title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 24, 2026
summary: Roughly 500 migrants who were relocated from Ceuta's El Trampolín beach camp on Aug 20 returned within hours and rebuilt a makeshift camp, forcing authorities to attempt a second eviction on Aug 21. Ceuta president Juan Vivas said moving people between locations in the city 'does not show a willingness to solve the problem,' and the city government warned it would suspend beach-cleaning operations if the cycle continued, citing crew safety. Migration Minister Elma Saiz said the government aims to expand reception capacity to roughly 4,000 places via four additional humanitarian sites. The Italy-Spain reciprocal Schengen border checks remain unchanged, still set to run to Sep 1 (Italy) and Sep 7 (Spain).

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: Spanish police began clearing the makeshift El Trampolín beach camp on Aug 20, relocating over 1,200 of roughly 4,000 migrants to two new temporary shelters, Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento. Human Rights Watch said on Aug 21 that Spain must urgently fix a 'humanitarian and rights crisis' after thousands spent nearly three weeks without adequate shelter or sanitation. Moroccan forces dispersed a 294-person regrouping attempt near Fnideq on Aug 16, the first sizeable new crossing bid since the July 30-31 surge. Spain is separately preparing a mainland transfer of roughly 500 unaccompanied migrant girls over EU objections, after several Spanish autonomous communities refused to accept minors from the crisis, and the EU announced it will boost Morocco border-control funding by an additional €190 million through 2027 as part of a pending partnership deal.
